title: Interval of Grateful Shade
description: Interval of Grateful Shade in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 949 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Evening Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: In-ter-val of grate-ful shade, Wel-come to my wea-ry head! Wel-come slum-bers to mine eyes, Tired with glar-ing van-i-ties!

lines: Thus I give my powers to rest.
Night and day his love the same!
Crown'st my days with various good;
Thy kind eye which cannot sleep,
Day and night I'm still with thee;
Guarded thus I sink to rest,

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
